title: Barnet's band stranded after the Huey Long incident
summary: Barnet's band plays New Orleans, offends Huey Long, and the musicians struggle home by mud roads while Barnet flies.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: That must have been '34. Barnet's band went to New Orleans and got tangled up with Huey Long. Huey Long hated the band.
Did someone do something to antagonize him?
Maybe it played too loud. Something of that nature.
Anyway, we were out from one
night to the next and we came wandering back to New York. Charlie, of course, had flew out, he didn't care.
He had plenty of money; he left us to our own devices.
There was a guitar player from Atlanta, Buff--I can't recall his name. A wife, little baby.

There were no interstates in those days, there were mud roads, and it rained. I remember going through Alabama and Mississippi and getting stuck in mud; no money, so we didn't sleep, I don't know what we ate.
I recall arriving at Washington and we stayed in a flop house, which you could do. This is in the middle of the Depression.
It wasn't that bad, but it was a flop house and everytime I go back I wonder where it was. I have no idea where it could have been.
It was one of those corner places.
